newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank/Portugal rate caution caps bond price moves.
newsitem.headline: Bank/Portugal rate caution caps bond price moves.

text.p: The reluctance of the Bank of Portugal to make further cuts to its money market rates is limiting room for further price gains at the short end of the curve as far as three-year government bonds (OT), analysts say.
The shorter end had already discounted a further easing in monetary policy before the end of the year and prices have little upside until the Bank delivers, they added.
"In these maturities, I am not going to increase my exposure. I am not going to sell, because I think money rates can fall further, but I will not buy until it happens," said one fixed-income trader.
The longer end of the curve will continue to track Spain as long as both countries are seen as firm candidates for the European Union's planned single currency, the analysts said.
Portugal is likely to continue to trade at a 15-25 basis point discount because of its better economic fundamentals, traders said.

"Yields up to the three-year OT have already discounted a cut in Bank of Portugal rates and therefore there will not be big (price) gains before the end of the year," said Mario Vigario of Morgan Grenfell in Lisbon.

Traders and analysts say that the Bank, which last cut its repo rate by 10 basis points to 7.00 percent on October 21, has room to lower the rate at least 25 basis points both for the repo and its draining rate.
The draining rate was last cut 40 basis points on April 19.
"Yields at the short-end have touched bottom. It makes no sense for them to fall further while the Bank does not lower rates," said a fixed-income trader at a large bank.

But the traditionally cautious central bank has been reluctant to move due to lingering concern over inflation, and traders said it may be waiting for some guarantees that wage rises will be severely restrained in 1997.
Wage restraint is seen as the key to pushing Portugal's average year-on-year inflation next year to under three percent which is likely to be the upper limit for qualifying for EMU.
"I think that the Bank has room to cut before the end of the year but it is unlikely to go beyond 25 basis points," said Mario Vigario.
